caption: 01 · PRACTICE — What already repeats?. Document the offer, client or audience promise, research method, design sequence, collaborator roles, quality threshold, payment path, correction route, and archive habit. Repetition reveals the institution already operating around the person.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 02 · RECORD — Can the practice prove what happened?. Use written scopes, invoices, contributor credits, versioned files, rights and permissions records, contact consent, expense evidence, tax records, and object identifiers appropriate to the actual jurisdiction and activity.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping can the practice prove what happened? within Can a Creator Build a House Before Building a Company?.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 03 · SEPARATE — Which formal questions cannot be solved by good habits?. Entity formation, liability, tax treatment, employment, insurance, securities, licenses, registrations, beneficial ownership, contracting authority, and cross-border activity require fact-specific professional review. A beautiful archive does not create a liability shield.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping which formal questions cannot be solved by good habits? within Can a Creator Build a House Before Building a Company?.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 04 · TRANSITION — What should move when structure arrives?. Inventory names, domains, accounts, agreements, equipment, files, marks, designs, licenses, debts, receivables, privacy obligations, and archive custody. Counsel and advisers must determine what can be assigned, licensed, contributed, retained, or newly contracted.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

caption: Celebrating “institution before company” can romanticize informal work, delay protections, conceal unpaid labor, or expose the creator and collaborators to avoidable risk. The point is not to postpone advice. It is to arrive with a legible practice map—and to formalize when the facts, jurisdiction, liability, tax, labor, funding, and continuity needs require it.
